question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume led to higher latency as the system struggled to handle the load.
why_chain: The rise in request volume caused the system to become overwhelmed.
The increased load required more instances to be scaled out.
The autoscaler's response to the load increase resulted in a temporary spike in latency.

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of catalog v3.20 likely introduced a new latency issue.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v3.20 occurred shortly before the change point.
The deployment may have introduced a new latency bug or configuration issue.
The new version of the catalog could have caused the system to behave differently, leading to higher latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of catalog v3.20 was the cause of the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment occurred hours before the change point, making it unlikely to be the cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler's response to the load increase was the cause of the latency spike.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler's response occurred after the change point, making it unlikely to be the cause.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region us-east rose from 137 ms to 270 ms (+97%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T04:40:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region us-east: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region us-east rose (2707 per 5 min before, 10491 per 5 min after, +288%).
At the same time, error rate for region us-east rose (0.40% before, 0.78% after, +97%).
Request volume 3x normal in us-east (us-east; 12 min after the change; record R009; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed catalog v3.20 to us-east (routine release) (catalog, us-east; 126 min before the change; record R008; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (us-east; 20 min after the change; record R010; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 126 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✗ The main factor does not rest on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change

actions.action: Roll back the catalog v3.20 deployment to revert any changes that may have introduced the latency issue.
Implement a more granular autoscaler to better handle the load and reduce latency spikes.
Monitor request volume and latency closely and take corrective action if the issue recurs.
